question: On Saturday morning the corner shop had 60 jars of marbles on its shelf. A delivery van dropped off 45 more jars before lunch, and during the lunch rush 102 jars were sold. In the afternoon a second delivery added 72 jars to the shelf. Every jar still on the shelf that evening contained exactly 8 marbles. Each of those marbles was worth 6 points in the shop's Saturday game. How many points were sitting on the shelf that evening?

Elena's tile workshop had 166 boxes of tiles in the yard, and Marcus delivered 20 more boxes, though he arrived half an hour late. The boxes were then shared equally among 3 building sites, and Elena's site took one share. At Elena's site 59 boxes turned out to be water damaged and were sent back to the supplier. Every box still at her site holds 6 trays. Each of those trays holds 8 tiles. How many tiles does Elena's site have?

At the Riverside charity walk, each of the 117 walkers raised 9 dollars from sponsors. A bake stall at the finish line brought in another 47 dollars. The route passed a dozen village halls along the river. All of the money raised was then divided equally among 5 local charities. The animal shelter, one of those charities, immediately spent 175 dollars on winter feed. How many dollars did the animal shelter have left?

Owen's recycling depot started the week with 198 crates of bottles, and his colleague Priya brought in 43 more, which was far fewer than Owen had collected on his own. Each of the depot's 4 lorries was then loaded with exactly that many crates. On the motorway 107 crates were damaged beyond use. A supermarket took 462 crates from the lorries, and a bottling plant collected another 154. How many crates were still on the lorries?

At dawn a farmer divided 144 apples equally among his 6 market stalls. At the stall by the fountain, the morning delivery van added 51 more apples. Just after noon a neighbour dropped off another 11 apples at that same stall. By evening the fountain stall had sold every one of its apples at 4 rupees each. How many rupees did the fountain stall take that day?

Mara planted 13 rows of carrots with 9 plants in every row. She later added 20 more seedlings to the same plot. She harvested 94 of the plants in August, rabbits destroyed 18 more, and she gave 4 plants to a neighbour. Her shed sits half a mile down the lane, and she has been gardening this plot for 15 years. Every plant still growing will produce 6 carrots. How many carrots can Mara still expect?

The radio station writes its schedule in minutes rather than in hours. For each of the 7 days of festival week, 230 minutes of music were planned. A special interview added another 71 minutes to the week's plan. By Friday night 1464 of the planned minutes had already been broadcast. The producer then cut 31 minutes from what was still to come. How many minutes of the plan were left?

Nina started the term with 95 stickers, and she traded 93 of them away to Owen, who ended up with far more stickers than she had. Owen felt guilty and gave her enough new ones to triple what she was still holding. Nina then split her stickers into 3 equal piles and kept only one pile, giving the others to her sisters. She lost 1 sticker on the walk home. At the weekend she bought 36 more. How many stickers does Nina have now?

Jonah rode 46 kilometres on each of the 5 days of his training camp. On the Saturday afterwards he rode another 44 kilometres. On Sunday morning he added 8 kilometres of warm-up laps, and on Sunday afternoon he rode a further 58 kilometres. His club records ride times in minutes rather than in hours, which fills his logbook with large numbers. How many kilometres did Jonah ride in total?

A church hall received 154 boxes of candles, and each box held 5 candles. A second delivery arrived that afternoon and doubled the number of candles in the store. A volunteer then donated 73 more candles. The hall counts its stock in single candles rather than in boxes, which the warden finds tedious. Over Christmas 540 candles were burned, and afterwards 33 unused candles were returned from the chapel. The hall itself was built 92 years ago. How many candles are in the store now?

Early in the morning a baker divided 30 kilograms of flour equally among his 3 ovens. Working with the flour set aside for one oven, he baked 4 loaves from every kilogram. In the afternoon each of those loaves was cut into 6 slices. He then packed all of that oven's slices equally into 5 paper bags. In the evening a school party ate 43 slices from one of those bags. The bakery weighs its flour in kilograms rather than in grams. How many slices were left in that bag?

A drinks depot began the month with 230 crates and took in 52 more from the bottling plant. Every crate in the depot holds 7 packs. Each pack contains 6 cans, and the depot always counts its stock in single cans rather than in crates. During the summer sale exactly half of all those cans were sold. How many cans were still in the depot?

A small museum's store held 229 old display cases, and 221 of them were sent away to another museum. Each case that stayed behind holds 5 fossils. A collector then donated 11 more fossils to the museum. The curator photographs every fossil in the collection from 6 different angles. A dozen visitors waited outside while she worked. How many photographs does the curator take?

On Monday morning a bookshop counted 6 display shelves with 97 books on each shelf. At midday a delivery added 21 books to those shelves. During the afternoon 269 books were sold from them. In the evening a school returned 70 books, all of which went straight back onto the same shelves. A dozen customers were still browsing when the shop closed. How many books were on those shelves at closing time?

A village choir had sold 16 tickets for its opening night by the end of January. It sold 70 more in February and another 15 in early March. Then 11 buyers cancelled, and a school block booking added 33 tickets. Every ticket costs 5 dollars, and the rehearsal begins half an hour before the doors open. The choir performed on 6 nights in all, and each night sold exactly that same number of tickets at that same price. How many dollars did the choir take altogether?

The Redhill cycling club stored 215 water bottles at its north depot, and a sponsor delivered 66 more to that same depot. The club keeps 2 depots in total, and the south depot holds exactly the same number of bottles as the north one. The club has been running for 38 years. At the spring race 91 bottles were handed out to riders. A charity later collected 242 bottles from the club. How many bottles does the club still have?

Amir had 25 pencils in his case, and 1 of them snapped in half and was thrown away. His classmate Bea gave him 59 pencils from a bulk pack she had bought, far more than Amir had started with. He handed 36 of those pencils to the younger class and left 5 of them in the art room. The school orders its pencils by the gross rather than by the single pencil. There are 28 desks in Amir's classroom. How many pencils are in Amir's case now?

Early on Saturday morning the community centre counted 144 chairs, and 2 of them were broken and taken away. Before lunch a neighbour lent the centre 30 more chairs. In the afternoon all the chairs were divided equally among the 4 halls. That evening 14 folding chairs were carried into the first hall, and a late delivery added another 64 chairs to that same hall. The centre lists its opening times in minutes rather than in hours on the noticeboard. How many chairs were in the first hall by the end of the day?

A school art teacher opened 5 pads of paper with 123 sheets in each pad. The sheets were shared equally among the 3 art classes. In one of those classes every sheet was cut into 4 greeting cards. Those cards were packed equally into 5 boxes, and the teacher spent half an hour tying them with ribbon. A parent then added 56 ready-made cards to one of the boxes. How many cards are in that box?

On Monday morning Tara had 45 jars of jam ready for the fair. She sold 25 of them at the early market. In the afternoon she made 68 more jars. Her sister Wendy had prepared exactly the same number of jars as Tara was holding by then, and the 2 sisters put all of their jars onto one stall. In the evening their father brought 18 extra jars to the stall. How many jars were on the stall that evening?

A podcast archive began the year with 183 episodes. The team recorded 32 more in the spring, then removed 82 old episodes that had gone out of date. A merger brought in 55 episodes from another show, and 39 bonus episodes were added in the autumn. The studio has 4 microphones on its desk. Every episode in the archive runs for exactly 9 minutes, and the archive states its total length in minutes rather than in hours. What is the total length of the archive in minutes?

Kofi counted 228 bricks in the yard, and Lena wheeled in 17 more, far fewer than Kofi had counted. A neighbour took 66 bricks away for a garden path, and 23 more were found to be cracked and were discarded. Each brick still in the yard weighs 8 kilograms. The yard always gives its loads in kilograms rather than in tonnes. What is the total weight, in kilograms, of the bricks left in the yard?

Hugo's laundry runs 3 identical vans, and on Monday each van collected 204 towels, all of which went into one pile. His colleague Sadia added 31 towels from the gym, a smaller load than any of the vans had brought. A hotel then sent 47 towels to the same pile, and a guesthouse sent another 47 later that day. The laundry weighs its work in kilograms rather than in pounds. How many towels were in the pile?

Bilal set out with 179 leaflets for the town fair. He handed 92 of them to shoppers on the high street, and the wind blew 48 more out of his bag. His friend Yara, who had started with far fewer leaflets than Bilal, gave him the 49 she still had. Each leaflet carries 9 coupons that can be torn off, and a dozen shops in town accept them. The fair runs for 3 days every summer. How many coupons was Bilal carrying?

A garden centre had 165 tulip bulbs in its store, and a supplier delivered 71 more. All of the bulbs were then shared equally among the 4 display beds. Squirrels dug up 7 bulbs from the first bed. The centre opened its new cafe 3 months ago. Every bulb still in the first bed will produce 2 flowers. How many flowers will the first bed produce?
